class.name: NNSTGuard
class.brief_description: Base class for all State Tree guard resources.
class.description: Guards decide whether a transition may be taken. Repeated evaluation of automatic transitions is driven by the trigger types a guard reports through [method get_supported_trigger_types]. Write a custom guard by deriving from this class in a script and implementing [method on_is_satisfied], plus [method on_get_supported_trigger_types] to say which changes make the result stale. The built-in guards evaluate themselves natively instead of using those hooks.

method.name: get_supported_trigger_types
method.description: Returns a bit mask of [enum NNSTRoot.TriggerType] values describing which changes can affect this guard's result. Automatic transitions use this to decide when they need to be re-evaluated. The base implementation asks the guard script for [method on_get_supported_trigger_types]; when that hook is missing it reports an error and returns [constant NNSTRoot.NONE], so the guard's transitions are only checked on [constant NNSTRoot.STATE_ENTER] unless the transition's guard composition reports additional trigger types.

method.name: is_satisfied
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the guard is satisfied, [code]false[/code] otherwise. Guards are used to determine if a transition can be taken or not. If the guard is satisfied, the transition can be taken. The built-in guards evaluate themselves natively; for a custom guard the result comes from [method on_is_satisfied]. When that hook is missing an error is reported and [code]false[/code] is returned.

method.name: on_get_supported_trigger_types
method.description: Implement this hook in a guard script to return the bit mask of [enum NNSTRoot.TriggerType] values that can change its result, as described in [method get_supported_trigger_types]. Built-in guards report their trigger types natively and never call this hook.

method.name: on_is_satisfied
method.description: Implement this hook in a guard script to decide whether the guard is satisfied, returning [code]true[/code] when the transition may be taken. [param transition] is the transition being evaluated and [param state] the state it belongs to. Built-in guards evaluate themselves natively and never call this hook.
